project_dependencies.use: PG36 selection, including the three meanings and the outer purchase/luk stage.
4.1.22 already interpreted; PG748 instantiates the case outputs and traces the two affix owners.
PG744 KS-18-HAV is the outer praise noun. Its inner offering relation remains credited there.
Ordinary masculine/neuter a and feminine ā case readouts.

source_observations.observation: Calf-benefiting milker and the camel illustration, with their negative contrasts. The semantic boundary is the following purchase relation.

source_observations.locator: Kāśikā 5.1.2, its three gaṇa clauses and examples
source_observations.observation: U-final stems, protective priority, the two nābhi senses, and two śvan lengths. The displayed ūdhanyaḥ kūpaḥ has an explicit well as head.

source_observations.locator: Nyāsa 5.1.2, from the uk question through ūdhanya
source_observations.observation: Both n retention and correlation of final accent with the long grade are explained. The wheel substitute depends on its particular yat.
Measure of a hundred palas versus ordinary wool. Nyāsa uses accent to distinguish direct mention of the stem from a yat derivation.
Two possible suffixes on named offering and cake examples. The literal havis has mandatory yat under 5.1.2.
Dvikambalyā and trikambalyā given in the contrast with the ī outcome for āḍhaka and for the horse collective.
source_observations.additional_locator: Padamañjarī ad 4.1.22, dvikambalyeti krītārthe ṭhañō luk

source_observations.observation: The selected outer ārhīya suffix undergoes luk on the operation-occasioned dvigu. The proper-name guard concerns the result.
Inner named wool taken as material for the finished blanket. The outer price is expressed with the instrumental dual.
One hundred palas, neuter si/am and kambalo ’sya syāt on the measure. Ordinary blanket-benefiting wool is feminine.

source_observations.locator: Haima Madhyamavṛtti with avacūri, part I, printed p.186, digital leaf 193
source_observations.observation: Names Haima ya at 7.1.34. Digitized note reports two other quantities, aśītiśata and ṣaṭṣaṣṭiśata, with anonymous attributions.
